store.summary: Model ham antennas with NEC2: SWR curve, gain, pattern, tune and cut list
store.description: From Ask Elmer, askelmer.com. A real antenna modeling lab in your pocket, running the NEC2 engine on the CardputerZero. Pick one of 18 antennas: half-wave dipole, inverted V, off-center-fed dipole, end-fed half wave, fan and trap dipoles, G5RV and ladder-line doublets, ground-mounted and elevated verticals, 5/8-wave and coil-loaded verticals, J-pole, Yagi (2 to 10 elements), Moxon, cubical quad, delta loop, horizontal sky loop and small magnetic loop. Set the frequency, height, wire and sizes in feet or metres, then Run: feed impedance, SWR into 50 ohm coax through the balun or transformer you pick, resonant frequency, 2:1 bandwidth, gain in dBi, takeoff angle, front-to-back and efficiency over real ground. See SWR across the band (or a wide sweep for multiband wires) and azimuth and elevation patterns. Tune for me adjusts the main size until the antenna is resonant, and the cut list tells you what to build. Optimize a Yagi for gain or front/back, see the coax loss and the SWR at the radio, and lay a real NanoVNA sweep (USB) or .s1p file over the model. Works offline. Keys 4-8: Run, Tune, SWR, Pattern, Cut. Fn+H shows help. Results are a model: trim and check the real antenna with an analyzer.
